cards.text: Friend, the writer of Hebrews has been telling his readers about a new covenant God promised (Hebrews 8:8-13). Now he looks back at the first covenant. It had rules for worship, plus a sanctuary right here on earth.

That tabernacle had two rooms: the Holy Place, with the lampstand, the table and the consecrated bread, and behind the second curtain, the Most Holy Place. That's where the gold-covered ark of the covenant sat, holding the stone tablets, the gold jar of manna and the budded staff of Aaron, Israel's first high priest. Above it were the cherubim of glory, but the writer says these things can't be discussed in detail now.

cards.question: With everything set up, the priests go into the first room regularly to do their sacred duties. Who goes into the second room, the Most Holy Place?

cards.text: And even the high priest goes in only once a year, never empty-handed. He makes an offering for himself and for the sins the people committed in ignorance.

cards.question: When the high priest goes into the Most Holy Place with his offering, he never goes in without ___.
Through this whole arrangement, the Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Most Holy Place had not yet been disclosed while the first tabernacle was still standing.

cards.text: The writer calls it an illustration for the present time. And the gifts and sacrifices offered there had a limit.

cards.question: The gifts and sacrifices offered in the tabernacle had a limit. What couldn't they do for the worshiper?

cards.text: Those gifts and sacrifices deal only with food and drink and special washings, outside rules. That's like polishing the outside of my oven till it SHINES and never touching the burnt crumbs inside.

cards.question: Those rules about food and drink and special washings were meant to stay in place forever.

cards.text: Friend, put the dough DOWN, because here comes the turn. Christ comes as high priest of the good things that have come.

cards.question: Christ, the high priest, goes through a tabernacle too. Which one?

answers.text: A greater one not made by hands
A grander one built of gold
A larger one built on Zion

cards.text: And Christ doesn't go in by the blood of goats and calves. Lean in for this one, friend.

cards.question: Christ doesn't use the blood of goats and calves. So how does He enter the Most Holy Place?
Like the high priest, Christ has to go back into the Most Holy Place every year.

cards.text: He entered once for all, friend. ONE time, and meanwhile it takes me three tries to get one batch right.

cards.question: By entering once for all with His own blood, Christ secured redemption that is ___.

cards.text: Now the writer reasons it out. If the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkled on people who are ceremonially unclean, make their bodies clean…
…how much more will the blood of Christ purify our consciences from works of death! Friend, that's the very thing those old gifts and sacrifices couldn't do.

cards.question: Through the eternal Spirit, Christ was offered unblemished to God. Who offered Him?

cards.text: Friend, He didn't just bring an offering. He WAS the offering.

cards.question: Christ's blood purifies our consciences so that we may serve the living God.
